service.description: Start an import of a GitHub repository (sourceRepository, owner/name) into a group (groupId), by the group's Owner with a confirmed address or an operator: into a repository of the group (repositoryId; one with issues or merge requests the import did not make is refused, numbersTaken, since numbers are kept) or a new one (slug, as wide as the group). token, a GitHub token that may read the repository, is kept encrypted for the run and dropped when it ends; the receipt keeps no trace of it. options: issues and pullRequests (both by default), and publishPrivate, without which a repository that is private on GitHub is refused (policyRefused) into a target wider than private. GitHub is asked for the repository first, before anything is locked or written: sourceRefused (Unprocessable) when it refuses the token or has no such repository. Conflict (importActive) while a run of the same source or into the same repository is active; limitReached past 2 active imports of the account or 5 of the site. The run then goes a step at a time (run#Import). Creates take operationId.

An import as its group's Owners and operators see it: its repository and source, its stage (queued, labels, issues, pulls, comments, links, done, failed, cancelled), counts by type (imported, source: seen at GitHub, failed), what could not be carried (reportList: sourceType, sourceId, errorText; notCarried: what is never carried, and reactions the forum does not have, by kind), waitingUntil while GitHub's rate limit holds it, running while a step runs, and revision.
The imports into a group (groupId), for its Owners, newest first, paged; with no group, every import of the site, for an operator.

Go on with a failed or cancelled import from where it stopped, or give a running one another token (token; needed once a run ended, since its token was dropped), with expectedRevision. Conflict while a step runs; notAvailable for a done import (start it again: what it has is not made twice, and what failed is tried again).

Stop an import where it is, with expectedRevision; its token is dropped. What it made stays, and it can be resumed with a token; a merge request of the git host a failed item left open (no conversation) is closed.

A repository's push mirrors, for its Maintainers: the address, the refs, whether it deletes refs the repository no longer has, enabled, hasCredential (never the credential), the last push, its result and error, and the next attempt (its error without any credential in it).

Make a push mirror (operationId) or change one (mirrorId), by a Maintainer with a confirmed address: url (https, with no credential in it), username and secret (a token; write-only, and not in the receipt), removeCredential (clears username and secret: the framework's clearCredential), hostKeyFingerprint, refs (ref patterns, comma separated; posted empty on a change, all branches and tags again: clearRefPattern), deleteRefs, enabled. Stored as the Maintainer, with authorization on: the framework keeps who gave the credential and pauses the mirror once that account is no longer a Maintainer. Unprocessable for an address the framework's outbound rules refuse, and secretRequired when a change of the address's host, its username or the host key does not give the secret again (or removeCredential).
Remove a push mirror, by a Maintainer.

Push a mirror now, by a Maintainer: queued. Conflict while a push of it runs. The framework's outbound check holds the pushes of a hidden repository. A failed push is told to the repository's Maintainers and Owners (handle#MirrorFailure).

A step of an import, as the account that started it (another account's call does nothing): at most budget API requests (10) from where its cursor is, each source item written in a transaction of its own, and the cursor saved. Nothing while GitHub's rate limit holds the run (waitingUntil) or while another step runs. The account must still own the group, else the run fails. Answers the stage, waitingUntil, the requests made and done once the run ended.

actions.script: const out = ec.resource.script("component://mr-mantle/service/mantle/smithy/Smithy.js").runImport({importId, budget}) stage = out.stage || null waitingUntil = out.waitingUntil || null requests = out.requests || 0 done = !!out.done

service.description: For the smithy_run_imports job: a step of each import that is due (its waitingUntil and leaseUntil past, read by the query), at most one of an account and two of a site in a pass, as the account that started it (ForumCore.asUser: signed in without a password for the step and out again without ending its own sessions); one whose account is gone or cannot sign in fails (accessLost) and its token is dropped. Each stands alone.

The framework's user-facade login sso-linked-service (MoquiConf.xml): told, after the commit of a real SSO sign-in that linked or confirmed the account's provider id, with authorization disabled. Records the proof (SmithyGithubLink) and claims the import's placeholders of that GitHub id (claim#GithubAccount), only when the flow is a GitHub one (an OauthFlow of type OctGitHub) whose endpoints are GitHub's own (its client type's defaults, urlsOverridden false, or exactly github.com's or an Enterprise Server's canonical addresses), providerHost is that GitHub's (api.github.com, or the Enterprise Server's host), and the account holds that id of that flow now. Anything else claims nothing; an edit of externalUserId by hand is no sign-in and calls nothing. Never fails: the framework logs a failure.

actions.script: claimed = ec.resource.script("component://mr-mantle/service/mantle/smithy/Smithy.js").ssoLinked({userId, authFlowId, providerHost, externalUserId, urlsOverridden: urlsOverridden === true}).claimed

service.description: For the SmithyMirrorFailure rule (entity/Smithy.eecas.xml): the framework told the account that stored a push mirror of its first failure after a success (a NotificationMessage of topic GitMirrorFailure, with no record); the other Maintainers and Owners of a repository Smithy keeps are told on the same topic, with the repository as its record, the error without any credential in it. Never fails the write: a failure is logged.

For the SmithyClaimOnMembership rule (entity/Smithy.eecas.xml): a membership of a site became active, so each account of the party claims, after the commit, the placeholders a sign-in already proved its GitHub id for (claim#GithubAccount without proven: only for a SmithyGithubLink of its id and flow now). Never fails the write: a failure is logged.

An account whose sign-in through a GitHub provider (an OauthFlow of type OctGitHub) linked a GitHub id (UserAccount.externalUserId) claims, in each site, the import's placeholder of that id: the account takes its GitHub login (SmithyAccount.githubLogin and githubUserId, so the agreement counts its imported commits) and its posts, issues, merge requests, assignments and reactions; the placeholder's profile ends. Only a placeholder of the GitHub the flow signs in with (its endpoints exactly GitHub's own: github.com's defaults or canonical addresses, or an Enterprise Server's own canonical ones on the placeholder's githubHost), for an id a sign-in proved (a SmithyGithubLink of the account's id and flow now, which only the sign-in hook handle#SsoLinked records), and only in a site where the account is an active member and not suspended; each site in a transaction of its own, one that fails logged and left. Safe to run twice; nothing for another provider.
